The 3rd Time’s a Charm: Nelson Brothers Reacquire Nelson’s Green Brier Distillery from Constellation Brands

  • Posted on November 17, 2026
  • By Distillery Trail
  • In Blog
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:38
Instaread

It’s not often in life you get a second chance to do something you love. It’s extremely rare for a third time to get a chance to do something you love but that is the way the family distilling business has panned out for brothers Andy and Charlie Nelson.

Back in the early 2020s during the Covid spirits boom, large corporations were buying craft distilleries left and right. One of those companies on the buying spree was Constellation Brands located in Rochester, New York. Now that the boom is over and sales have slowed for the last two years in a row, some of these larger companies are rethinking their strategy and paring down their ownership of these smaller distilleries to focus on their larger opportunities.

Constellation Brands Sells Distillery Back to Original Owners

Stay Informed: Sign up here for the Distillery Trail free email newsletter and be the first to get all the latest news, trends, job listings and events in your inbox.

Brothers Andy and Charlie Nelson restarted the family’s distilling business that dates back to the 1800s. The original Nelson Greenbrier Distillery business was started by their great-great-great grandfather in 1860. That business was shut down in 1909 when Tennessee voted in Prohibition, a decade before national Prohibition.

In 2012, the Nelson brothers rekindled the family business when they started Nelson’s Green Brier Distillery in Nashville, Tennessee. In 2016, Constellation’s venture capital group liked what they saw in the Tennessee based distillery and made a minority investment in the brand. In 2019, they extended that investment to take a 75% majority investment in the business and followed that up in 2024 with a full acquisition.

Brothers Andy and Charlie remained active in the business until Charlie departed in 2023 followed by Andy in 2024 after Constellation obtained full ownership. When they departed they were able to purchase the rights to Belle Meade Bourbon and Louisa’s Liqueur under their new umbrella company Belle Meade Spirits. Belle Meade Bourbon is a brand the brothers created when they first started their distillery using sourced bourbon from companies like MGP and Bardstown Bourbon Co. Louisa’s Liquor is a coffee caramel flavored pecan liqueur.

Andy and Charlie Nelson Retake Family Ownership of Nelson’s Green Brier Distillery

14 years after it all began for the Nelson brothers, ownership of Nelson Greenbrier Distillery has returned to family ownership for the third time. The Nelson brothers have acquired full ownership of the distillery and inventory of Nelson’s Green Brier Tennessee Whiskey and Nelson Brothers Bourbon. The agreement also includes taking over the lease agreement of the 50,000 square-foot distillery, event space and production facility at 1414 Clinton St. in Nashville.

“This has been our family business dating back to the 1800s, so to have the opportunity to once again have full ownership of the brand and its storied history is extraordinarily meaningful to us,” said Andy Nelson, co-founder of Nelson’s Green Brier Distillery.

“There will certainly be a transition period where we determine next steps for the brand, our portfolio of products and the distillery itself, but our intention is to get us back to our roots of honoring our rich family heritage as quickly as possible by producing premium spirits right here in our own hometown that reflect the craftsmanship, history and passion of the original distillery our great-great-great grandfather started.”

Charlie Nelson, co-founder of Nelson’s Green Brier Distillery, echoed his brother’s excitement for the next chapter in the brand’s storied past, adding, “In a city where we continue to see more and more outside companies choose Nashville as part of their expansion plans, it’s so fun to be able to have this opportunity to once again operate Green Brier as a locally owned family business. This city has given so much to us, and we see this as an opportunity to give back by continuing to invest in the community we call home.”

Under its new leadership, Nelson’s Green Brier Distillery plans to continue business as usual with all existing staff retained and the restaurant, bar, tours and events proceeding as normal. The Nelson family says they are committed to the brand’s long-term stability and growth in the years ahead.

Charles Nelson first established the original Green Brier Distillery in 1870, becoming one of the most successful distilleries in the country as Tennessee’s largest pre-Prohibition distillery and producer of the original Tennessee Whiskey. In 1909, Prohibition became law in Tennessee, and the distillery was forced to close. Nearly 100 years later, Charles’ great-great-great grandsons, Andy and Charlie Nelson, discovered this family history, rebuilt the distillery and began producing Nelson’s Green Brier Tennessee Whiskey using the original pre-Prohibition recipe.

In 2006, Andy and Charlie Nelson stumbled upon the discovery that their great-great-great grandfather, Charles Nelson, was the founder of Tennessee’s largest pre-Prohibition distillery and produced the original Tennessee Whiskey. The distillery’s history dates back to 1860 and in 2019, Nelson’s Green Brier Distillery bottled the first batch of Green Brier Tennessee Whiskey since 1909. The modern-day distillery, located at 1414 Clinton St. Nashville, TN 37203, is open to the public seven days a week and offers guided tasting experiences as well as an event space and gift and bottle shop.
